prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1049; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Claimant reports being struck on the driver side by an insured vehicle that entered the intersection on a late yellow. Claimant states they were transported from scene by ambulance and diagnosed with a concussion. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Initial contact made by phone; claimant is cooperative and has provided basic incident details.

Entry 2: Obtained the police report from the responding agency. It notes both drivers gave conflicting accounts of the signal phase. Scene photos show damage concentrated on the claimant's driver door and the insured's front bumper. Traffic camera request submitted to the municipality, response pending. Advised claimant of their right to seek legal counsel and that they may choose to have a representative present for any recorded statement.

Entry 3: Recorded statement taken from claimant. Claimant reports headache, dizziness, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating since the collision. Claimant has an upcoming appointment with a neurologist and has provided the name of the treating physician. Requested medical authorization forms and prior records for the past five years to evaluate any pre-existing condition. Claimant agreed to sign the forms.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the emergency department confirming a concussion diagnosis with recommended rest and follow-up. Records note the claimant was alert and oriented on arrival. Reviewed the insured's statement, which indicates the insured did not see the signal change and believed the light was green. Liability appears to lean toward the insured based on the physical evidence and the police narrative, pending the camera footage.

Entry 5: Followed up with claimant regarding treatment progress and time missed from work. Claimant reports still experiencing symptoms but attending therapy sessions. Explained the claims process and next steps, including the timeline for a settlement evaluation once treatment stabilizes. Claimant has been given the adjuster's direct contact information. Diary set to review the traffic camera response and updated medical status in thirty days.
